title: End-Guadalupian (Capitanian) mass extinction
summary: Occurring around 260 million years ago near the end of the Guadalupian (Capitanian) epoch, this severe extinction eliminated 74–80% of terrestrial vertebrate genera in southern Africa alongside catastrophic losses among marine reef builders and brachiopods globally. Associated with flood-basalt volcanism of the Emeishan Large Igneous Province, it reorganized terrestrial tetrapod communities and marine ecosystems just eight to ten million years before the even larger end-Permian mass extinction.

uncertainty.note: Start is the late Capitanian terrestrial extinction pulse dated to 260.259 ± 0.081 Ma in the Karoo Basin (Day et al. 2015); end is the Guadalupian-Lopingian boundary (base of Wuchiapingian) at 259.51 ± 0.21 Ma (ICS Chart 2024/12; 259.857 ± 0.084 Ma at the Penglaitan GSSP).

importance.justification: The end-Guadalupian mass extinction wiped out 74–80% of terrestrial vertebrate genera and decimated marine carbonate ecosystems, demonstrating that major biotic crisis accompanied the Emeishan volcanism prior to the Permian-Triassic boundary.
